### 23. Lord of Miracles

**Port:** Lima, Peru
**Date:** Sat Oct 2 – Mon Nov 1
**Flags:** CULTURE, FOOD

The principal procession days are Oct 18, 19, and 28; the largest Catholic procession in South America and one of the largest religious gatherings in the world, dating in continuous form to 1687. October is the Mes Morado (Purple Month) in Lima, the entire historic city center decorated in purple banners, ribbons, and chains; thousands of Limeños wear purple robes for the duration. The 2-ton silver palanquin holding the replica of the 1651 image of Christ (painted by an Angolan slave on an adobe wall in Pachacamilla, said to have miraculously survived three earthquakes including the 1746 tsunami that destroyed Lima) is carried through the historic center by 33-man cuadrillas of bearers in 30-minute shifts across roughly 24 hours of cumulative procession across the four days. The principal procession on Oct 18 begins at 6 a.m. from the Monasterio de las Nazarenas and reaches the Iglesia del Carmen around 1 a.m. the following morning, followed by the National Police, Firefighters’ Corps, and Peruvian Army honor guards.

**The Berth.** Belmond Miraflores Park; the Country Club Lima Hotel in San Isidro. Hotel B in Barranco for the canonical Lima heritage 1914 Belle-Époque boutique by Relais & Châteaux in the artist’s quarter; JW Marriott Hotel Lima in Miraflores on the Pacific cliff for the canonical modern luxury with the ocean view; Casa Andina Premium Miraflores for the canonical Lima modern dependable.

**The Galley.** In Lima for the festival-season eating: Central by chef Virgilio Martinez in Barranco for the canonical Lima World’s 50 Best modern Peruvian (the canonical Andean-elevation tasting menu); Maido by chef Mitsuharu “Micha” Tsumura for the canonical Lima Nikkei modern Peruvian- Japanese; Astrid y Gastón by chef Gastón Acurio for the canonical Lima modern Peruvian institution; La Mar Cebichería for the canonical Lima ceviche destination. Festival-specific: turrón de Doña Pepa (the cinnamon-honey nougat made specifically for this season), mazamorra morada (the purple corn pudding), and anticuchos (skewered beef-heart) at every street stall along the procession route.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Historic Centre of Lima* (Lima, Peru). The Spanish colonial centre founded 1535 by Pizarro, the Plaza Mayor framed by the Palacio de Gobierno, the cathedral, and the Archbishop's Palace with its carved wooden Mudéjar balcony; UNESCO 1988 after the surviving baroque
2. *San Francisco Monastery & Catacombs* (Lima, Peru). The seventeenth-century yellow-and-white Franciscan monastery with the Mudéjar wooden coffered ceiling, the catacombs below holding the skeletal remains of an estimated 25,000 Limeños buried during the colonial period; the library upstairs holds 25,000 antique books

### 24. Goose Fair

**Port:** Forest Recreation Ground, Nottingham, UK
**Date:** Wed–Sun first weekend of October
**Flags:** CULTURE

One of the oldest charter fairs in Europe and the most significant annual gathering in the East Midlands cultural calendar, observed each first weekend of October on the Forest Recreation Ground in central Nottingham. The 731st annual edition. The fair traces continuously to October 1284 when King Edward I granted a Royal Charter to the Borough of Nottingham permitting an annual market on the Feast of Saint Edmund, held to coincide with the autumn driving of geese from the Lincolnshire fens to London markets via Nottingham (the name derives from the 19th-century practice of selling thousands of geese on the fair’s opening day). The modern fair has been continuous except for the 1646 Civil War cessation, the 1665 plague year, and the World Wars. The 19th century saw the transformation from a pure trade fair into a pleasure fair with mechanical rides; today the fair operates as Britain’s largest traveling funfair, with 500+ rides and stalls including the traditional rides (the Wall of Death, the Helter Skelter, the Galloping Horses carousel). Signature foods: mushy peas served in china bowls, hot-roast pork sandwiches with crackling and apple sauce, candy floss, and the iconic Nottingham brandy snaps. 500,000+ visitors over five days; the opening-night ceremonial bell-ringing by the Lord Mayor at 6 p.m. on Wednesday officially begins the fair.

**The Berth.** In Nottingham: Hart’s Hotel on Standard Hill for the canonical Nottingham design-set boutique walking distance to the Goose Fair site; The Park Plaza Nottingham on Maid Marian Way for the canonical modern downtown dependable; Lace Market Hotel in the converted 19th-century Lace Market warehouse for the canonical heritage Nottingham boutique.

**The Galley.** In Nottingham: Restaurant Sat Bains at Trentside by chef Sat Bains for the canonical Nottingham two-Michelin-star modern British (the canonical East Midlands destination); Hart’s Restaurant on Standard Hill by chef Tim Hart for the canonical Nottingham modern British; Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem on Brewhouse Yard at the foot of Nottingham Castle since 1189 (the oldest inn in England, where Crusaders mustered for the Holy Land) for the canonical Nottingham heritage pub destination.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Nottingham Castle* (Nottingham, England, UK). The seventeenth-century ducal mansion built on the bedrock cave-honeycombed ridge where Robin Hood is said to have run rings around the Sheriff, the seven-hundred-year-old caves still tunneling beneath the city; the castle reopened 2021 as Nottingham's museum
2. *Sherwood Forest* (Edwinstowe, Nottinghamshire, England, UK). The ancient royal hunting forest of the Norman kings, the 1,000-year-old Major Oak still standing on its prop-frame in the Birklands at the centre, said to be Robin Hood's hideout; 1,045 acres of pollarded oak woodland kept as a National Nature Reserve

### 25. Greenwich Village Halloween Parade

**Port:** Sixth Avenue, Greenwich Village, NYC
**Date:** Sun Oct 31
**Flags:** CULTURE, ART

The world’s largest Halloween parade and one of the major annual queer-and-arts event in the New York calendar, observed each Halloween night (Oct 31) along Sixth Avenue from Spring Street to West 16th Street in Greenwich Village. The 54th annual edition. Founded in 1973 by Greenwich Village mask-maker and Off-Broadway puppeteer Ralph Lee as a small neighborhood walking trick-or-treat parade for his young children’s friends, the parade has grown across five decades into the only major American parade in which every participant is also a performer (there is no audience-vs.-marcher distinction; anyone in costume may join the parade at any of the lineup zones). 60,000+ costumed marchers process up Sixth Avenue, watched by 2 million+ spectators lining the route, broadcast live on NY1, and televised internationally. Three signature elements: (1) the giant puppets, 50+ enormous papier-mâché puppet figures built each year by Ralph Lee’s successor puppet workshop, the visual signature of the parade since 1973; (2) the theme, each year’s parade has a different unifying theme announced two weeks in advance; (3) the music, 50+ marching bands, samba schools, and drum corps along the route. The parade begins at 7 p.m. sharp at Sixth Avenue and Spring Street; arrival by 5 p.m. for prime viewing positions, especially the customary Sixth Avenue-and-West-8th-Street spectator zone.

**The Berth.** In Greenwich Village walking distance to the parade route: The Greenwich Hotel in Tribeca by Robert De Niro for the canonical Lower-Manhattan design-luxury (already noted on September V10 San Gennaro); The Marlton Hotel on West 8th Street for the canonical Greenwich Village boutique-heritage; The Jane Hotel on Jane Street for the canonical heritage 1908 boutique on the West Village waterfront.

**The Galley.** In Greenwich Village: Carbone on Thompson Street for the canonical NYC red-sauce; Don Angie in the West Village for the canonical NYC modern Italian-American; Babbo on Waverly Place for the canonical Greenwich Village Italian; Joe’s Pizza on Carmine Street for the canonical NYC late-night slice; Caffe Reggio on MacDougal since 1927 for the espresso machine that introduced cappuccino to America.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Washington Square Arch* (Greenwich Village, New York, USA). Stanford White's 23-metre Tuckahoe marble arch raised 1892 at the foot of Fifth Avenue, modelled on Paris's Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel for the centenary of Washington's inauguration; the marble figures of Washington in War and Peace added 1916 and 1918
2. *Stonewall National Monument* (Greenwich Village, New York, USA). The small triangular Christopher Park opposite the Stonewall Inn where the June 1969 uprising began the modern gay-rights movement; the Stonewall Inn made a National Historic Landmark in 2000 and the first U.S. National Monument for LGBTQ history in 2016

### 1. Día de los Muertos

**Port:** Throughout Mexico
**Date:** Mon–Tue Nov 1–2
**Flags:** CULTURE

UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage; the Mexican Day of the Dead, when families build elaborate ofrendas (altars) decorated with marigold petals, sugar skulls, papel picado, photos of the deceased, and the favorite foods and drinks of the departed, cemetery vigils through the night of Nov 1–2 with picnics, candles, and music. Oaxaca and Pátzcuaro are the most spectacular celebrations; the Mexico City parade, created for the 2015 James Bond film Spectre and now the largest Día de Muertos event in the world, is the Saturday before.

**The Berth.** Mexico City: Las Alcobas; Four Seasons; Casa Habita. Oaxaca: Quinta Real; Los Amantes. Yucatán: Chablé Yucatán; Hacienda Temozón. Hotel Carlota on Río Amazonas in Cuauhtémoc for the canonical Mexico City design-boutique; Casa Polanco in the converted 1940s mansion for the modern luxury near Bosque de Chapultepec. In Pátzcuaro for the canonical Day-of-the-Dead pilgrimage: Hotel Mansión Iturbe in central Pátzcuaro for the heritage 17th-century courtyard boutique on the plaza.

**The Galley.** Mexico City: Pujol; Quintonil; Sud 777; Contramar. Oaxaca: Casa Oaxaca; Origen; Las Quince Letras. Yucatán: Kuuk in Mérida; Hartwood in Tulum. Rosetta in Roma Norte by chef Elena Reygadas for the canonical CDMX modern Italian-Mexican; Maximo Bistrot by chef Eduardo García for the canonical Mexico City modern Mexican farm-to- table; Pasillo de Humo in Roma Norte for the canonical Oaxacan-comfort cooking in CDMX.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Templo Mayor* (Mexico City, Mexico). The Aztec twin-shrine pyramid at the heart of Tenochtitlán uncovered 1978 beneath the Zócalo, the shrines of Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc rebuilt in seven concentric stages between 1325 and 1521; the museum holds the eight-tonne carved Coyolxauhqui stone unearthed by accident in 1978
2. *Frida Kahlo Museum / Casa Azul* (Coyoacán, Mexico City, Mexico). The cobalt-blue family house in Coyoacán where Frida was born 1907 and died 1954, the kitchen kept exactly as she left it; her wheelchair still by the easel, the ashes in a pre-Columbian urn on the four-poster

### 2. Día de Muertos in Oaxaca

**Port:** Oaxaca, Mexico
**Date:** Sun–Tue Oct 31 – Nov 2
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

October 31 through November 2; Oaxaca’s Day of the Dead is the most photographed and most visited in Mexico, but the food angle is what brings the cooks: pan de muerto in every panadería (anise-and-orange-blossom egg bread shaped with bone crossbones), mole negro on the family ofrenda alongside the pumpkin candy and chocolate, hot chocolate ground from local Tabasco beans on the metate. Eat at Casa Oaxaca (Alejandro Ruiz), Origen (Rodolfo Castellanos), Las Quince Letras for the seven moles, and the Mercado 20 de Noviembre’s Pasillo de Carnes Asadas for the smoke-and-grill lunch. The candlelit cemeteries at San Felipe and Xoxocotlán on the night of November 1, bring a respectful silence.

**The Berth.** Quinta Real Oaxaca in the converted 16th-century convent; or Hotel Azul in the centro histórico; or Los Amantes for the boutique courtyard. Grana B&B in Centro Histórico for the canonical Oaxaca design-boutique walking distance to the Zócalo; Pug Seal Oaxaca in the converted 18th-century townhouse for the heritage boutique near Santo Domingo.

**The Galley.** Casa Oaxaca (Alejandro Ruiz) for contemporary Oaxacan; Origen (Rodolfo Castellanos) for the modern interpretation; Las Quince Letras for the seven moles; the Mercado 20 de Noviembre Pasillo de Carnes Asadas for the smoke-and-grill lunch. Levadura de Olla by chef Thalia Barrios García for the canonical Oaxaca modern indigenous; Itanoní on Av. Belisario Domínguez for the canonical Oaxacan tlayuda and heirloom-corn tortilleria.

1. *Monte Albán* (Oaxaca, Mexico). The Zapotec capital raised on a flattened mountaintop above Oaxaca around 500 BCE, the Danzantes carved-stone figures the first writing in Mesoamerica; UNESCO 1987, the central plaza still aligned to the equinoxes
2. *Mitla* (Oaxaca, Mexico). The Mixtec-Zapotec ceremonial city east of Oaxaca whose Group of the Columns is covered in fourteen distinct geometric mosaic patterns cut from 100,000 individual stones without mortar; the place of the dead in Nahuatl

### 3. Eat Drink SF

**Port:** Multiple venues across San Francisco
**Date:** Sat–Sun Oct 30 – Nov 7, 9 days
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

The most prestigious restaurant-industry-organized food festival in the Western United States, central to San Francisco’s culinary identity, nine days each November when the city’s restaurant-industry trade association uses every kitchen in the city to demonstrate why San Francisco is, dish for dish, dollar for dollar, one of the most exceptional food cities in the world. The festival is operated by the Golden Gate Restaurant Association (GGRA), the storied 90-year-old San Francisco restaurant-industry trade association founded in 1936, making the GGRA one of the oldest restaurant trade associations in the United States, whose mission across nearly a century has been to celebrate and empower the restaurant community through advocacy, education, marketing, events, and training. The GGRA’s role in San Francisco’s food scene is genuinely irreplaceable: the association serves the city’s 4,000+ restaurants on labor and tax policy, lobbies City Hall on industry-wide issues (the post-COVID re-opening protocols, the minimum-wage debates, the outdoor-dining-permit framework).

**The Berth.** The Fairmont on Nob Hill; The Battery in the Financial District; or Inn at the Presidio for the budget. Hotel Drisco in Pacific Heights for the canonical 1903 boutique heritage; 1 Hotel San Francisco on Mission Street for the modern sustainable-luxury on the Embarcadero; The Proper San Francisco in Mid-Market for the design-set Kelly Wearstler luxury.

**The Galley.** Zuni Café for the roast chicken; Tartine Manufactory in the Mission; Liholiho Yacht Club for the Hawaiian-fusion; Saison for the splurge. Mister Jiu’s in Chinatown by chef Brandon Jew for the canonical SF Michelin-starred modern Chinese-American; Hilda and Jesse in North Beach by chefs Kristina Liedags Compton and Rachel Sillcocks for the canonical SF brunch destination.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Golden Gate Bridge* (San Francisco, California, USA). Joseph Strauss's 1937 Art Deco suspension bridge linking the city to the Marin headlands, the Pacific weather rolling fog under the deck most summer afternoons; the south tower 227 metres of riveted steel above the cold green water
2. *Ferry Building* (San Francisco, California, USA). The 1898 grey-sandstone clock tower at the foot of Market Street, the city's central transit hub before the bridges, now the country's most photographed farmers' market and food hall; the 75-metre tower modelled on the Giralda of Seville

### 5. Pushkar Camel Fair

**Port:** Pushkar, Rajasthan, India
**Date:** Tue–Mon Nov 9–15
**Flags:** CULTURE, FOOD

One of the largest livestock fairs in the world, held annually in late October/November in the desert town of Pushkar, Rajasthan, in the days surrounding the full moon of Kartik Purnima. 50,000 camels, horses, and cattle traded over five days, alongside religious bathing in the sacred Pushkar Lake (one of the holiest pilgrimage sites in Hinduism, host to one of the few temples to Brahma anywhere on Earth). Camel races, longest-mustache contests, turban-tying competitions, and the trademark sunset balloon rides over the white temple-ringed lake.

**The Berth.** Udaipur: Taj Lake Palace on Lake Pichola; Jaipur: Rambagh Palace; Jodhpur: Umaid Bhawan Palace; Jaisalmer: Suryagarh. In Pushkar itself, book the festival year ahead: The Sunset luxury tent camp on Mela Ground for the canonical festival-base immersive tented stay; Ananta Spa & Resorts Pushkar for the canonical modern festival-base resort on the outskirts; Pushkar Bagh Resort for the heritage-style Rajasthani fort hotel.

**The Galley.** Udaipur: 1559 AD for canonical Rajasthani; Jaipur: Suvarna Mahal at Rambagh; Anokhi Café for everyday; Jodhpur: Indique at Pal Haveli; Jaisalmer: Saffron at Hotel Nachana Haveli. In Pushkar (all vegetarian per the sacred-city rule): Sunset Café on Pushkar Lake for the canonical festival-week sunset thali; Out of the Blue on Sadar Bazar for the canonical Pushkar all-day continental-and-Indian; Honey & Spice for the canonical Pushkar South Indian dosa breakfast.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Mehrangarh Fort* (Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India). The 122-metre cliff fortress raised by Rao Jodha in 1459 above the blue-painted houses of Jodhpur, the carved sandstone galleries above with the cannonball-scarred outer walls still visible from the lanes below; still owned by the Rathore royals
2. *Amber Fort* (Jaipur, Rajasthan, India). The pink-and-yellow sandstone hill-fortress of the Kachhwaha rajas, raised from 1592 on a ridge above Maota Lake; the Sheesh Mahal mirror chamber inside with thousands of fragments forming a constellation when a single candle is lit

### 6. Barbados Food & Rum Festival

**Port:** Various venues across Barbados
**Date:** Thu–Sun Nov 4–7
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

The 19th annual edition; the Caribbean’s most prestigious culinary festival, the apex food event in the West Indies, and one of the great food-and-drink pilgrimages on the world calendar, a four-day immersion in the cuisine, rum culture, and Bajan hospitality of the country that has been making rum longer than any other place on Earth. Founded in 2009 by the Barbados Tourism Marketing Inc. (BTMI) to showcase the island’s unique fusion of African, English, Indian, Portuguese, and Indigenous Arawak culinary heritage alongside its 350+ year rum-making tradition. Winner of Caribbean’s Best Culinary Festival at the World Culinary Awards in both 2023 and 2024. The festival’s foundational claim is geographic and historical: Barbados is the birthplace of rum. The first known reference to “rumbullion” (the proto-name for rum) appears in a 1651 description of Barbados; the world’s oldest commercial rum distillery, Mount Gay Distilleries, was deeded in 1703 (the deed itself dating the operation to before that year, making it 320+ years of continuous production); and the West Indies Rum Distillery (founded 1893) is the oldest continuously-operating rum distillery in the world.

**The Berth.** Sandy Lane in Holetown (the iconic 1961 luxury anchor, where Frank Sinatra and Tiger Woods married, the festival’s most prestigious accommodation partner); the Sandpiper Hotel on Holetown Beach (boutique luxury, 50 suites, a festival headline venue). Cobblers Cove, a Relais & Châteaux hotel in Speightstown for the canonical Barbados boutique-luxury heritage on the Platinum Coast; The Crane Resort on the southeast coast since 1887 for the canonical Barbados heritage grand-dame.

**The Galley.** The Cliff for canonical seafood-on-the-cliff; Cin Cin by the Sea for modern Caribbean; Oistins Fish Fry on Friday for the local; Mustor’s Restaurant for cou-cou and flying fish. The Tides in Holetown for the canonical Barbados modern Caribbean fine-dining on the beach; Champers Restaurant on the south coast for the canonical Bajan modern continental with the canonical Friday-night cou-cou; Brown Sugar in Aquatic Gap for the canonical Bajan buffet lunch.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Mount Gay Distilleries* (St Michael, Barbados). The Mount Gay rum estate near Saint Lucy on the north of the island, deeded in 1703 and so the oldest commercially active rum producer on Earth by recorded title; the modern still house still pulling fresh molasses through copper to the same recipe
2. *Bridgetown & its Garrison* (Bridgetown, Barbados). The Georgian harbour-town and the early British Caribbean garrison around the Savannah parade ground; UNESCO 2011, the cobbled wharf where rum, sugar, and the English navy met for three centuries

### 7. Taste of Abu Dhabi

**Port:** Gateway Park North, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi, UAE
**Date:** Fri–Sun Nov 12–14
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

An annual three-day pattern, in its fifth year; the Emirate’s flagship consumer food festival and the marquee public-facing event in Abu Dhabi’s increasingly serious culinary calendar, founded in 2023 by MENA Live Events as the Abu Dhabi sister to the established Taste of Dubai (the global Taste festivals format originating in London 2004 and now running in 20+ cities worldwide), Taste of Abu Dhabi has grown to 19,000+ attendees over the three days and become the principal showcase for the city’s restaurant scene against the spectacular backdrop of Yas Island, the same engineered island that hosts the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Ferrari World, Yas Waterworld, Yas Mall, and the Etihad Arena. The festival format is the Taste model adapted for the Gulf: 15 of the city’s most acclaimed restaurants (a curated mix of Time Out Abu Dhabi Restaurant Awards winners, established names, and notable newcomers) build temporary kitchens at Gateway Park North, each serving a curated menu of three-to-five tasting-portion dishes including one Taste Exclusive created specifically for the weekend and unavailable elsewhere, designed so attendees can graze across the entire city’s cooking in three days. Recent rosters have included Fouquet’s Abu Dhabi (the Parisian institution’s UAE outpost) and Catch by St.

**The Berth.** Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental on the Corniche; The St. Regis Saadiyat Island; or Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat Beach. Erth Abu Dhabi at the converted Armed Forces Officers Club for the canonical Abu Dhabi modern luxury with the Yas Island view; W Abu Dhabi, Yas Island at the Yas Marina Circuit for the canonical F1-themed festival-immersive base.

**The Galley.** Hakkasan Abu Dhabi at Emirates Palace; Coya at the Four Seasons for Peruvian; Beach House at Park Hyatt; Al Mrzab for canonical Emirati. Niri by Yannick Alléno at Erth Abu Dhabi for the canonical Abu Dhabi modern French; Mezö at the St. Regis for the canonical Abu Dhabi modern Mediterranean.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque* (Abu Dhabi, UAE). The white-marble mosque completed 2007 with 82 domes and the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world, 5,627 square metres woven by 1,200 weavers in Mashhad; the third-largest mosque on Earth, the seven minarets a different gold at dawn
2. *Louvre Abu Dhabi* (Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi, UAE). Jean Nouvel's 2017 Universal Museum under a 180-metre dome made of 7,850 metal stars, the rain of light filtering through to the white pavilions below; the second of the two Louvres anywhere, on a lease until 2037

### 8. Pirates Week Festival

**Port:** Throughout the Cayman Islands
**Date:** Nov 12–28

Cayman Islands’ national cultural festival, founded 1977, 17 days of pirate-themed events on Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac, and Little Cayman, including the iconic Pirate Landing on the George Town waterfront, the Heritage Days exploring traditional Caymanian culture, the Float Parade, fireworks displays, sea-shanty performances, and the closing Cardinal D Memorial Concert.

Palm Heights on Seven Mile Beach for the canonical Cayman design-set Gabriella Khalil-designed boutique; The Westin Grand Cayman Seven Mile Beach Resort for the canonical festival-week modern dependable.

**The Galley.** Blue by Eric Ripert at the Ritz-Carlton; Camana Bay’s Mizu for the Asian; Cracked Conch by the Sea for the canonical seafood; Vivine’s Kitchen for the local Caymanian. Avecita by chef Marius Karner at Camana Bay for the canonical Cayman modern small- plates; Tukka in East End for the canonical Cayman Australian-Caribbean fusion with the local catch.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Cayman Crystal Caves* (Old Man Bay, Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands). The three open chambers of the limestone cave system carved by water in the bluff above Old Man Bay on Grand Cayman's north side, stalactites the colour of caramel and an underground lake at the bottom of the third cave
2. *Stingray City* (North Sound, Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands). The waist-deep sandbar in the North Sound where Atlantic southern stingrays gather to be fed by visitors, fishermen having cleaned conch there for generations before tourists noticed; the rays here entirely free-ranging, not enclosed

2. *Haedong Yonggungsa Temple* (Busan, South Korea). The 1376 Goryeo-era seaside temple east of Busan, the prayer hall built on cliffs above the rocky tideline of the East Sea, the 108-step descent to the courtyard ending at the bronze sea-goddess Haesu Gwaneum on her rock outcrop

### 10. Loy Krathong & Yi Peng Lantern Festival

**Port:** Thailand (esp. Chiang Mai)
**Date:** Nov 13–14
**Flags:** CULTURE, FOOD

Two simultaneous full-moon festivals in northern Thailand, held on the November full moon. Loy Krathong (national, observed across Thailand) sees small banana-leaf rafts carrying flowers and candles released onto rivers and lakes as offerings to the water spirits. Yi Peng (specific to Lan Na/Northern Thailand) sees thousands of paper sky lanterns released into the night sky over Chiang Mai, in the most photographed Thai image of the year. The mass release at Mae Jo University outside Chiang Mai is ticketed; smaller releases at temples across the city are free. Three days of food fairs, street parades, and the Chiang Mai contest for the most beautiful krathong.

**The Berth.** 137 Pillars House in the historic 19th-century compound; or Anantara Chiang Mai Resort on the Ping; or U Chiang Mai inside the moat. Four Seasons Resort Chiang Mai in Mae Rim for the canonical Chiang Mai luxury rice-paddy resort; The Dhara Dhevi Chiang Mai for the canonical Lanna-themed luxury resort with the 60-acre temple-replica grounds; Raya Heritage on the Ping River for the canonical Chiang Mai modern design-luxury by Boon Rawd Brewery.

**The Galley.** Khao Soi Khun Yai for the canonical northern noodle; Sailomjoy for khao soi by the river; David’s Kitchen for European; the Sunday Walking Street market for everything else. Le Du Chiang Mai by chef Thitid “Ton” Tassanakajohn for the canonical Chiang Mai modern Thai (sister to the Bangkok original); Hong Tauw Inn in the Nimman district for the canonical Lanna home-style cooking; Tong Tem Toh for the canonical Chiang Mai street-stall northern-Thai institution.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Wat Phra Singh* (Chiang Mai, Thailand). Chiang Mai's most revered temple, founded 1345 to house a buddha image that may or may not have come from Sri Lanka; the gold leaf flaked on the prayer hall's red lacquer, the chanting at four every morning
2. *Sukhothai Historical Park* (Sukhothai, Thailand). The thirteenth-century capital of the first Thai kingdom, brick stupas and lotus-bud chedis rising from the lily ponds; UNESCO 1991, the place where the Thai script and the wai were born

Held at the actual Kryal Castle medieval-themed attraction, a fully built castle complex 90 minutes northwest of Melbourne, full lists jousting on a permanent tournament field, multiple combat tournaments, falconry displays, period archery, Saturday-night feast in the great hall (separate ticket), and the iconic Saturday-night fire show across the castle ramparts.

### 12. Hospices de Beaune Wine Auction

**Port:** Beaune, Burgundy, France
**Date:** Sun Nov 21
**Flags:** FOOD

Burgundy’s three-day November feast culminating in the world’s most prestigious charity wine auction, held at the 15th-century Hôtel-Dieu in Beaune since 1859 and now run by Christie’s. 800+ barrels of the year’s Côte d’Or Premier and Grand Cru wines from the Hospices’ own 60-hectare estate sell to the highest bidders; proceeds fund the historic charitable hospital. The Saturday Glorious Banquet at Clos de Vougeot, the Sunday Pauléé de Meursault, black-tie, white-tie, and the burgundies of the year.

L’Hôtel de Beaune on Rue Belin for the canonical Beaune heritage boutique; Abbaye de Maizières in the converted 12th-century Cistercian abbey for the canonical Beaune heritage Cistercian- cellar luxury walking distance to the Hôtel-Dieu.

2. *Cîteaux Abbey* (Saint-Nicolas-lès-Cîteaux, Burgundy, France). The 1098 mother house of the Cistercian Order founded by Robert of Molesme, the order from which the Burgundian wine regions were tended for seven centuries; the abbey still functioning, the original abbey church gone but a small museum kept

### 14. Katara Traditional Dhow Festival

**Port:** Katara Cultural Village, Doha, Qatar
**Date:** Wed–Sat Nov 24 – Dec 4, ~10 days
**Flags:** CULTURE, PIRATE

The 17th annual edition of Qatar’s flagship heritage celebration; ten days each late November on the corniche beach at the Katara Cultural Village, the country’s purpose-built cultural campus on the West Bay shore. Established in 2011 as a deliberate act of cultural memory in a country that pivoted from pearl-diving and dhow-trade to natural gas in a single generation, the festival is the most authentic showcase of Qatari maritime heritage on the calendar. The programme: traditional dhow races between teams of pearl-diving captains in the lateen-rigged sambuk and shu’ai-class wooden vessels that built Qatar’s pre-oil economy; pearl-diving demonstrations with only nose clips and stone weights; live boat-building on the beach where Qatari and Omani shipwrights shape teak hulls with adze and chisel; traditional Khaleeji music and Ardha sword-dance; falconry showcases with saker and peregrine falcons; Saluki hunting-dog displays; and the kitchen-tent circuit serving balaleet, machboos, thareed, and harees. Pair with the Museum of Islamic Art, the National Museum of Qatar, Souq Waqif for the evening, and a desert-safari to Khor Al Adaid.

**The Berth.** The Chedi Katara Hotel & Resort directly on the Katara Cultural Village grounds for the boutique-luxury festival-route stay; the St. Regis Doha at Pearl-Qatar for the grand-luxury anchor on the artificial pearl island; the Mandarin Oriental Doha at Msheireb for the modern-downtown five-star at the heritage quarter; the Four Seasons Hotel Doha at West Bay for the canonical business-luxury with the Corniche view; or any of the Souq Waqif Boutique Hotels for the heritage-quarter stay.

**The Galley.** IDAM by Alain Ducasse at the Museum of Islamic Art for the most architecturally spectacular fine-dining in the Gulf (the I.M. Pei building’s top floor with the Corniche view); Hakkasan Doha at the St. Regis for the canonical Cantonese-luxury circuit; Argan at Souq Waqif for the Moroccan tagines and pastilla; Bandar Aden in Souq Waqif for the canonical Yemeni mandi (slow-roasted lamb on saffron rice); Parisa at Souq Waqif for white-tablecloth Persian on a hand- painted-tile setting; Saasna for the Qatari home-style cooking nearly impossible to find in restaurant form; and any karak chai stop on Al Corniche Street for the canonical Qatari afternoon

**The Bearings.**

1. *Museum of Islamic Art* (Doha, Qatar). I. M. Pei's 2008 cream-limestone museum on its own artificial island in Doha Bay, the geometric massing of cubes-on-cubes inspired by the medieval Ibn Tulun ablutions fountain in Cairo; the largest collection of Islamic art under a single roof
2. *Souq Waqif* (Doha, Qatar). The restored nineteenth-century Bedouin market in central Doha, the alleys of carpenters, falconers, spice-sellers, and tailors rebuilt 2006 over the original site, the falcon hospital at the back the busiest in the world

### 15. Armistice Day at Verdun

**Port:** Douaumont Ossuary & Verdun, Lorraine, France
**Date:** Thu Nov 11
**Flags:** CULTURE

The 109th anniversary of the WWI armistice; ceremonial mass at the Douaumont Ossuary holding the unidentified remains of 130,000 French and German soldiers, Last Post and the Marseillaise at the Memorial of Verdun, period reenactor units of the French Army of 1916 in horizon-blue uniform, and joint Franco-German wreath-laying. The most emotionally charged Armistice Day observance in continental Europe.

**The Berth.** Paris: Hôtel de Crillon, Le Meurice, Lutetia. Provence: La Bastide de Gordes; Hotel Crillon le Brave. Burgundy: Le Cep in Beaune; Loire: Domaine des Hauts de Loire. In Lorraine near Verdun: Hôtel Les Jardins du Mess in Verdun itself for the canonical festival-base in the converted 19th-century officers’ mess overlooking the Meuse; Hôtel de Vogüé in central Verdun for the canonical heritage boutique. In Metz (1 hour east): La Citadelle, an MGallery hotel in the converted 16th-century military fortress for the canonical Lorraine heritage luxury. In Nancy (1.5 hours south): Grand Hôtel de la Reine on Place Stanislas for the canonical 18th-century Belle- Époque grand-dame.

**The Galley.** Paris: Le Comptoir du Relais; Septime; L’Arpège; Frenchie. Provence: La Mirande in Avignon; Baumanière. Burgundy: Lameloise in Chagny; Loire: Le Choiseul in Amboise. In Lorraine: Le Coq Hardi in Verdun for the canonical Verdun heritage 1827 traditional restaurant with the canonical Meuse-region truite; Le Mas in Metz by chef Christophe Dufossé for the canonical Metz Michelin-starred modern Lorraine. In Nancy: La Maison dans le Parc by chef Françoise Mutel for the canonical Nancy Michelin-starred modern Lorraine.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Douaumont Ossuary* (Verdun, Lorraine, France). The 137-metre concrete cloister-and-tower of 1932 holding the unidentified bones of 130,000 French and German soldiers killed in the ten-month battle of 1916, visible through the small grilled windows along the base of the building
2. *Memorial of Verdun* (Fleury-devant-Douaumont, Lorraine, France). The museum and battlefield centre opened 1967 on the site of the destroyed village of Fleury, taken and retaken sixteen times in 1916, never resettled; the steel-and-glass extension of 2016 cantilevered above the cratered earth still visible all around

### 17. Iceland Airwaves

**Port:** Central Reykjavík, Iceland
**Date:** Tue–Sat Nov 2–6, 5 days
**Flags:** ART, CULTURE

The most consequential music festival in Iceland and the centerpiece of the global indie-music discovery calendar, observed annually over five days in early November across central Reykjavík. Founded 1999 by Icelandair as a marketing initiative to boost off-season tourism, the festival evolved into the typical European discovery showcase for emerging artists. 25,000+ attendees from 90+ countries; 200+ artists across 30+ venues simultaneously throughout the city center (Harpa Concert Hall, Gamla Bíó, Iðnó, KEX Hostel). Iceland Airwaves has been the international launch point for Björk, Sigur Rós, Of Monsters and Men, Kaleo, Ásgeir, and Daði Freyr. The festival operates on the “single wristband, all venues” model, attendees walk the central streets between sets, often catching 8–12 acts in a single night. The November setting (8 hours of daylight, the first snow, the Northern Lights visible from the city outskirts) is itself the festival.

**The Berth.** In Reykjavík: The Reykjavik EDITION on Austurbakki for the modern luxury (the canonical festival-flagship at the heart of the venue circuit); Hotel Borg on Austurvöllur for the heritage 1930 Art-Déco grand-dame; Sandhotel on Laugavegur for the design-set boutique on the main shopping street. Pre/post-fest: ION Adventure Hotel in Nesjavellir for the canonical geothermal- lagoon extension; Deplar Farm in the remote Tröllaskagi for the Eleven Experience canonical Northern Lights luxury.

**The Galley.** In Reykjavík: Dill for the canonical Michelin-starred New Nordic; Matur og Drykkur in the harbour for canonical Icelandic comfort food (the fish-skin chip, the dried fish snacks); Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur for the canonical late-night lamb hot dog; Sumac on Laugavegur for the canonical Reykjavík modern Middle Eastern; Kaffivagninn at the old harbor for the canonical Reykjavík fishermen’s-café breakfast (the oldest restaurant in Iceland).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Þingvellir National Park* (Bláskógabyggð, Iceland). The open-air parliament site of the Icelandic Commonwealth, the Öxará waterfall feeding the rift lake, the Drekkingarhylur drowning pool where adulteresses were sentenced under the old law; one of the few places on Earth where two tectonic plates can be walked between
2. *Blue Lagoon* (Grindavík, Iceland). The opalescent geothermal pool in a lava field 40 minutes from Reykjavík, water heated to 38 °C by the Svartsengi power plant next door, white silica mud kept in buckets at the lagoon edge for self-application; 1992 the year it opened to the public

### 18. Lewes Bonfire Night

**Port:** Lewes, East Sussex, UK
**Date:** Fri Nov 5
**Flags:** CASTLE, CULTURE

The most spectacular and most genuinely consequential Guy Fawkes Night observance in Britain, observed annually on November 5 in the medieval Sussex market town of Lewes (population 17,000, on the River Ouse below the South Downs). The Lewes Bonfire Night is the largest non-commercial bonfire celebration in the world, observed continuously since the 1605 Gunpowder Plot. Six Bonfire Societies (Cliffe, Commercial Square, Borough, Southover, Waterloo, and South Street) maintain rival 600-year-old traditions. Each society has its own elaborate costumes, including the distinctive smuggler’s costume sets, and constructs its own elaborate effigies each year (typically the Pope, current political figures, contemporary villains). Five processions converge through the medieval streets carrying torches and effigies, parading to the High Street where the effigies are then ceremonially burned at separate bonfires across the town. 80,000+ visitors fill the small town for the night; train service from London Victoria is the archetypal route in; advance accommodation booking essential.

**The Berth.** In Lewes itself: Pelham House Hotel on St Andrew’s Lane for the canonical Lewes heritage 16th- century boutique walking distance to the procession routes; Shelleys Hotel on the High Street for the canonical heritage 17th-century coaching inn. Nearby: The Black Horse Inn in Rottingdean for the canonical Sussex coaching-inn alternative (20 minutes south); The Grand Hotel Eastbourne on the East Sussex coast for the canonical Belle-Époque grand-dame option (30 minutes south).

**The Galley.** In Lewes: Limetree Kitchen on Lewes High Street for the canonical Lewes modern British seasonal; Riverside Café on the River Ouse for the canonical Sussex riverside breakfast; Bill’s Restaurant (Lewes flagship of the chain Bill Collison founded here in 2000); The Snowdrop Inn on South Street for the canonical Lewes festival-night pub fortification before the procession.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Beachy Head & Belle Tout Lighthouse* (East Sussex, England, UK). The 162-metre chalk headland east of Eastbourne, the highest sea cliff in southern England, the 1832 lighthouse moved 17 metres inland in 1999 ahead of the retreating cliff; the red-and-white modern lighthouse stands in the sea below
2. *Glyndebourne* (East Sussex, England, UK). The country opera house founded 1934 by John Christie in the grounds of his Tudor manor near Lewes, the only opera festival in Britain where evening dress is the convention and the long picnic-interval the heart of the day

### 19. Beaujolais Nouveau

**Port:** Beaune, Lyon & the Beaujolais region / worldwide
**Date:** Thu Nov 18, the 3rd Thursday
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

The most consequential annual wine release in the global calendar, observed each third Thursday of November simultaneously across France and 110 countries worldwide. Beaujolais Nouveau is the fresh young red wine produced from Gamay grapes in the Beaujolais region of southern Burgundy, released only weeks after the September harvest in a tradition dating to the 1951 inauguration of the official release date by the French government. The festival’s signature moment: midnight Thursday morning when the wine is officially released; bars and restaurants across France and the global Beaujolais Nouveau circuit (Tokyo, NYC, London, Hong Kong, Bangkok) open simultaneous parties featuring the year’s first taste. Marketing slogan: “Le Beaujolais Nouveau est arrivé!” Beaune, the signature Burgundy festival town, holds the largest French celebration; the cellars of Georges Duboeuf in Romanèche-Thorins (the defining Beaujolais producer, founded 1964) is the original home. 65 million bottles released globally on the day.

**The Berth.** In Beaune: Hôtel Le Cep on Rue Maufoux for the canonical Beaune Relais & Châteaux heritage in the 14th-century mansion; L’Hôtel de Beaune for the heritage boutique. In Lyon (90 minutes north): Cour des Loges in Vieux Lyon for the canonical Lyon Renaissance-buildings luxury. In Mâcon (40 minutes south for the heart of Beaujolais): Château de Pizay for the canonical Beaujolais wine-country heritage in the 14th-century medieval-castle hotel.

**The Galley.** In Beaune: Maison Lameloise in Chagny (15 minutes south) for the canonical three-Michelin-star Burgundian; Le Carmin for the heritage modern Burgundian. In Mâcon: L’Aubépin by chef Cyril Laugier for the canonical Mâcon modern Burgundian. In Lyon: any bouchon for the canonical Lyonnaise Beaujolais Nouveau release ritual (the canonical Daniel et Denise on Rue Créquy for the canonical Lyon bouchon by chef Joseph Viola).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Hôtel-Dieu de Beaune* (Beaune, Burgundy, France). The 1443 hospice with multicoloured glazed-tile roof and the Salle des Pôvres still set with its 28 medieval beds, the Last Judgement polyptych still on the chapel altar; the wine auction held in the great salle every third weekend of November since 1859
2. *Clos de Vougeot* (Vougeot, Burgundy, France). The walled 50-hectare Cistercian vineyard given to the monks of Cîteaux in the twelfth century, the great château built within the wall in 1551 still home to the Chevaliers du Tastevin and the Saturday-night banquet of the Trois Glorieuses

### 20. Bon Om Touk

**Port:** Phnom Penh, Cambodia
**Date:** Mon–Wed Nov 22–24
**Flags:** CULTURE

The most spectacular and most genuinely consequential annual festival in Cambodia, observed each November on the full moon of Kadeuk in the Khmer lunar calendar in Phnom Penh on the confluence of the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. The Water and Moon Festival celebrates the unique annual reversal of the Tonlé Sap River, the only river on Earth that changes direction with the seasons, flowing into the great Tonlé Sap Lake during the monsoon and reversing each November as the monsoon ends and the lake’s waters drain back into the Mekong. The festival’s signature events: (1) the Bandet Pratip, the illuminated float parade at night on the Tonlé Sap, with massive electrically-lit floats sponsored by government ministries and major companies, processing past the Royal Palace; (2) the Bun Om Touk dragon boat races during the day, with 400+ canoes from across Cambodia competing in the defining 60-rower long-boat race over a 1.5-km course on the Tonlé Sap; (3) the Sampeah Preah Khae (moon prayer) at midnight on the second night, when families gather to offer the essential amok rice cakes to the moon for the harvest’s blessing. 2 million+ pilgrims fill Phnom Penh for the three days; the city’s traffic is closed.

**The Berth.** In Phnom Penh: Raffles Hotel Le Royal on Rukhak Vithei Daun Penh for the canonical 1929 grand-dame heritage luxury (where Jackie Kennedy stayed in 1967); Rosewood Phnom Penh on Sothearos Boulevard for the modern luxury riverfront with the panoramic Mekong-confluence view; The Plantation Urban Resort & Spa on Street 184 for the canonical Phnom Penh design- set boutique in the converted colonial mansion.

**The Galley.** In Phnom Penh: Malis on Norodom Boulevard by chef Luu Meng for the canonical Phnom Penh modern Khmer; Romdeng on Street 174 by trainees of Friends International for the canonical Khmer modern with the social mission (the canonical tarantulas, red-ant beef-and-prahok); The Russian Market food stalls for the canonical Phnom Penh street-food destination (the canonical kuy teav noodle-soup breakfast).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Angkor Wat* (Siem Reap, Cambodia). The early-twelfth-century Khmer temple-mountain begun by Suryavarman II as the Vishnu sanctuary of his royal capital, the largest religious monument on Earth, the bas-reliefs of the Churning of the Sea of Milk still telling the story 800 metres long; UNESCO 1992
2. *Royal Palace & Silver Pagoda* (Phnom Penh, Cambodia). The 1860 royal palace of the King of Cambodia, the Throne Hall topped by the Preah Tineang Tevea Vinichhay coronation tower, the Silver Pagoda inside the inner compound floored with 5,329 silver tiles and holding an emerald Buddha of Baccarat crystal

### 1. Art Basel Miami Beach

**Port:** Miami Beach Convention Center
**Date:** Wed–Sun first weekend of December
**Flags:** ART

The most prestigious contemporary-art fair in the Americas, founded 2002 as the American sister of Art Basel Switzerland, 280 leading galleries from across 30+ countries showing major works at the Convention Center, plus parallel art weeks taking over the rest of Miami Beach (Design Miami, NADA, Untitled, Scope, Pulse, plus public installations across South Beach and the Miami Design District). The week’s parties run all night.

**The Berth.** The Setai on South Beach; Faena Miami Beach for the Baz Luhrmann production; or The Standard on Belle Isle for the boutique. ### 3. Austerlitz Reenactment

**Port:** Slavkov u Brna, Czech Republic
**Date:** Sat–Sun nearest Dec 2
**Flags:** CULTURE, CASTLE

The 222nd anniversary of Napoleon’s masterpiece against the combined Russian and Austrian armies in 1805, known as the Battle of the Three Emperors; thousands of reenactors in French, Russian, and Austrian uniforms across the original Pratzen Heights, mounted Cossacks and chasseurs, line infantry maneuvering in period drill, the Cairn of Peace as backdrop. The largest Napoleonic-era reenactment in Central Europe and a December-anniversary counterpart to the June Waterloo reenactment.

**The Berth.** Prague: Augustine, Aria Hotel, or the Carlo IV. In Brno: The Barceló Brno Palace or Grandezza Hotel Luxury Palace. In Brno near Slavkov: International Brno on Husova for the heritage Brutalist Czech grand-dame; Hotel Royal Ricc on Stará for the canonical Brno heritage 17th-century townhouse boutique in the medieval old-town center.

**The Galley.** Prague: Field; La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise; U Kroka for canonical svíčková; Lokál for the pilsner-and-pork institution. Brno: Pavillon for the modern Czech. In Brno: Borgo Agnese by chefs Pavla and Honza Pijáček for the canonical Brno modern Czech- Italian; Atelier Cocktail Bar & Bistro on Veveří for the canonical Brno design-set modern small-plates.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Cairn of Peace* (Mohyla míru, Prace, Czechia). The 26-metre Art Nouveau pyramid raised 1912 on Pratecký kopec, the Pratzen Heights at the centre of the 1805 battlefield, the four sarcophagi at the base for the Russian, Austrian, and French dead; the first peace monument ever raised on a European battleground
2. *Tugendhat Villa* (Brno, Moravia, Czechia). Mies van der Rohe's 1930 white-steel-and-glass house on a Brno hill, the open plan and disappearing window walls and onyx partition still as they were on opening day; UNESCO 2001, the first modernist domestic building inscribed

### 4. Krampusnacht & Krampuslauf

**Port:** Alpine Austria, Bavaria, South Tyrol
**Date:** Sun Dec 5
**Flags:** CULTURE

December 5–6 across the Alpine arc (Austria, Bavaria, South Tyrol, and Slovenia). The Krampus, Saint Nicholas’s horned goat-demon companion, runs through Alpine villages on the night of December 5 (Krampusnacht) and the morning of December 6, swinging birch switches and rattling chains to terrify children who have been bad. The runs (Krampuslaüfe) are organized by traditional Krampusgruppe, costumed groups in elaborate hand-carved wooden masks, sheepskin and goat-fur cloaks, cowbells the size of small church bells. The largest runs are in Bad Mitterndorf (Austria), Salzburg, Kaltern (South Tyrol), and the Bavarian villages south of Munich. Pair with Christkindlmärkte by day.

**The Berth.** Vienna: Hotel Sacher; Hotel Imperial on the Ring; 25hours Hotel Wien at MuseumsQuartier. Salzburg: Hotel Sacher Salzburg; Goldener Hirsch. In South Tyrol for the Kaltern Krampuslauf: Adler Spa Resort Dolomiti in Ortisei for the canonical Dolomites luxury; Romantik Hotel Stafler in Mauls for the canonical South Tyrol heritage 17th-century post-station boutique.

**The Galley.** Vienna: Steirereck im Stadtpark; Figlmüller for canonical Wiener Schnitzel; Café Central for the coffee-house ritual; Gasthaus Pöschl for the Beisl. Salzburg: Triangel near the Festspielhaus; St. Peter Stiftskulinarium. In South Tyrol: St. Hubertus at Rosa Alpina in San Cassiano by chef Norbert Niederkofler for the canonical Dolomites three- Michelin-star “Cook the Mountain” tasting; Pretzhof in Tulfer near Sterzing for the canonical Alpine farmhouse traditional South Tyrolean.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Salzburg Old Town* (Salzburg, Austria). The seventeenth-century baroque city of the prince-archbishops in the bowl of the Salzach valley, the Mirabell Gardens and the Residenzplatz and the Getreidegasse on the right bank, the Hohensalzburg fortress brooding above; UNESCO 1996
2. *Hallstatt* (Hallstatt, Upper Austria). The salt-mining village on the steep western shore of Lake Hallstatt, the 7,000-year-old salt mine still working in the mountain above, the village layered onto the cliff so tightly there is no road through; UNESCO 1997

### 5. Seoul Lantern Festival

**Port:** Cheonggyecheon Stream & Gwanghwamun Plaza, Seoul
**Date:** mid-December through early January 2028, ~3 weeks
**Flags:** CULTURE, ART

The 19th annual edition; Seoul’s signature winter cultural festival and one of the most beautiful urban light installations on Earth, the moment when the South Korean capital, in the middle of its coldest months, transforms a 1.3-kilometer downtown stream and the surrounding palaces into an open-air gallery of traditional hanji paper lanterns and contemporary LED light art that draws 2.5–3 million visitors per edition. Founded in 2009 to celebrate the “Visit Korea Year 2010–2012” tourism promotion campaign as a five-day exhibition along Cheonggyecheon Stream, the festival was so successful in its first edition that public pressure (largely from international tourists) extended it to seven additional days, and the event was made annual immediately after. Over the past 16 years it has grown into a month-spanning winter cultural moment that runs from mid-December through the first days of January, encompassing Christmas, the Western New Year, and the Korean New Year holiday window. The festival changed its Korean name to Seoul Bitchorong Festival (“Seoul Light-Lantern Festival”) in 2014 to reflect the expansion from purely traditional lanterns into a hybrid display incorporating modern LED light art, and since 2022 has expanded geographically beyond the Cheonggyecheon Stream to include Gwanghwamun Plaza in front of the 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace.

**The Berth.** Four Seasons Seoul in Gwanghwamun; The Shilla in Jung-gu for the heritage; or Le Méridien Seoul Myeongdong for the central; or Boutique Glad in Yeouido. Josun Palace, a Luxury Collection Hotel in Gangnam for the modern luxury in the Josun-dynasty-themed flagship; JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square Seoul for the canonical Gwanghwamun-adjacent festival-base.

**The Galley.** Mingles (Kang Min-goo) for modern Korean kaiseki; Jungsik for the Seoul-Manhattan two-star; Gwangjang Market for bindaetteok and yukhoe; Hadongkwan in Myeongdong for gomtang. Hansikgonggan by chef Cho Hee-sook for the canonical Seoul modern Korean royal-cuisine tasting; Tosokchon Samgyetang in Gyeongbokgung for the canonical Seoul ginseng-chicken- soup destination (a 5-minute walk from Gwanghwamun Plaza).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Gyeongbokgung Palace* (Seoul, South Korea). The 1395 main palace of the Joseon dynasty at the foot of Bugaksan, burned by the Japanese invasion of 1592 and burned again by the colonial occupation, restored from the foundations through the 1990s and 2000s; the changing of the royal guards three times a day
2. *Changdeokgung Palace & Secret Garden* (Seoul, South Korea). The 1405 secondary Joseon palace where the kings lived for most of the dynasty after Gyeongbok burned, the Huwon Secret Garden behind it a 32-hectare hill garden of pavilions and lotus ponds; UNESCO 1997

### 7. Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day

**Port:** USS Arizona Memorial, Oahu, Hawaii
**Date:** Tue Dec 7
**Flags:** CULTURE

December 7, the 86th anniversary of the 1941 Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor that brought the United States into World War II. The USS Arizona Memorial at the World War II Valor in the Pacific National Monument hosts the annual ceremony (the bell of the USS Arizona rings at 7:55 AM, the moment the attack began). Survivors, dignitaries, and family members attend; the National Park Service operates the visitor center and the boat shuttles to the memorial. Pair with the USS Missouri Memorial nearby (where the war ended) and the Pacific Aviation Museum on Ford Island.

### 9. Naples at Christmas

**Port:** Naples, Italy
**Date:** mid-to-late December
**Flags:** FOOD, CULTURE

Mid-to-late December; the most dramatic Christmas in Italy. Struffoli (honey-glazed dough balls) and baccalà (salt cod) on every table; Christmas Eve’s Festa dei Sette Pesci (Feast of the Seven Fishes) prep begins on December 20. Via San Gregorio Armeno’s presepi workshops produce hand-carved nativity figures year-round but reach fever pitch in December, the politicians, footballers, and pop-culture figures added to the standard scene each year are the running commentary on the Italian year. Late-night pizza pilgrimages to Da Michele or Sorbillo close out every evening; midnight Mass at the Duomo holds the dried blood of San Gennaro.

**The Berth.** The Grand Hotel Vesuvio on the Lungomare; or the Romeo Hotel in the porto for the modernist option. Hotel Excelsior Vittoria in Sorrento (45 minutes south) for the canonical Bay-of-Naples Belle-Époque grand-dame on the Sorrentine cliffs; Casa Angelina on the Amalfi Coast for the canonical December-extension luxury at Praiano.

Palazzo Petrucci on Piazza San Domenico for the canonical Naples Michelin-starred modern Campanian; Concettina ai Tre Santi by Ciro Oliva in the Sanità district for the canonical Naples modern pizza (a worthy Christmas-week pilgrimage).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Pompeii* (Pompeii, Campania, Italy). The Roman city buried by Vesuvius on August 24, 79 CE under metres of pumice and ash, kept whole by the sealing, the bread still in the ovens; UNESCO 1997 with Herculaneum
2. *Cappella Sansevero* (Naples, Campania, Italy). The eighteenth-century private Sansevero chapel hidden in central Naples, Giuseppe Sanmartino's 1753 Veiled Christ inside, the marble shroud carved so finely the eye refuses; the alchemist prince Raimondo di Sangro's anatomical machines in the crypt below

### 10. Mevlana Whirling Dervishes

**Port:** Mevlana Mausoleum, Konya, Türkiye
**Date:** Tue–Fri Dec 7–17, climax Fri Dec 17
**Flags:** CULTURE, ART

The 754th annual commemoration of the death of Jalál ad-Dín Muhammad Rūmí (1207–1273), the Persian-language poet and Sufi mystic whose mausoleum in Konya is the spiritual heart of Anatolian Islam and one of the world’s great pilgrimage sites. Rumi called his death Şeb-i Arus, the “Wedding Night,” because he viewed it as his reunion with the Beloved (the Divine), and his last instruction to his disciples was to mourn his passing not as a loss but as a wedding feast. The 10-day festival leading up to the anniversary of December 17, 1273 is the world’s deepest annual concentration of Sufi spiritual practice. The Mevlevi Order, the “Whirling Dervishes,” was founded by Rumi’s son Sultan Veled and his disciples in the years after the master’s death; their distinctive Sema ceremony (the white robe representing the shroud, the tall conical hat representing the gravestone of the ego, the right palm raised to receive divine grace, the left palm lowered to pour it back to earth, the slow rotation that becomes a meditative ecstasy) was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2008. Pair with the Alaeddin Mosque on the Seljuk citadel hill, the İnce Minareli Medrese, the Karatay Medrese tile museum, and a three-hour drive south through the Anatolian plateau to Cappadocia.

**The Berth.** Hich Hotel Konya in the historic Mevlana district for the boutique-design heritage anchor; Bera Mevlana Hotel for the modern-luxury stay closest to the shrine; Dedeman Konya Hotel & Convention Center for the canonical business-luxury. Cappadocia side trip: Argos in Cappadocia in Uçhisar; Museum Hotel in Uçhisar; or Carus Cappadocia in Ortahisar. Istanbul arrival/departure: Pera Palace Hotel Jumeirah (the Agatha Christie and Orient Express grande- dame since 1892), the Four Seasons Hotel Istanbul at Sultanahmet, or Çιrağan Palace Kempinski on the Bosphorus.

**The Galley.** In Konya: Gülbahçesi Konya Mutfağι for the canonical etli ekmek (the city’s signature thin lamb-and-flatbread); Mevlevi Sofrasι near the mausoleum for the Mevlevi-tradition vegetarian Sufi cuisine; Konak Konya Mutfağι for the Anatolian classical. In Istanbul: Mikla on the rooftop of the Marmara Pera for Mehmet Gürs’s modern-Anatolian flagship; Asitane in Edirnekapι for the

**The Bearings.**

1. *Hagia Sophia* (Istanbul, Türkiye). For a thousand years the largest enclosed space on earth, its dome seeming to hang from heaven on a chain of light; church, then mosque, then museum, then mosque again, Hagia Sophia has outlived every empire that claimed it
2. *Mevlana Mausoleum* (Konya, Türkiye). The turquoise-tiled tomb of Jalal ad-Din Rumi, the thirteenth-century Persian poet and the founder of the Mevlevi Sufi order, still the most visited religious shrine in Türkiye; the Whirling Dervishes still perform the sema in his honour each December

### 12. Edinburgh Hogmanay

**Port:** Edinburgh, Scotland
**Date:** Thu–Sat Dec 30 – Jan 1
**Flags:** CULTURE

Edinburgh’s three-day New Year celebration (December 30 – January 1), Scotland’s national new-year festival and one of the largest year-end celebrations in Europe. The Torchlight Procession on December 30 winds 20,000 torch-bearers from Edinburgh Castle down the Royal Mile to a fireworks finale at Calton Hill. The Hogmanay Street Party on December 31 fills Princes Street with 75,000 ticketed revelers, three live music stages, and the midnight fireworks over the Castle. The Loony Dook on January 1 sends thousands into the freezing Firth of Forth in costume.

**The Berth.** The Balmoral on Princes Street, the Walter Scott of grand hotels; or The Witchery by the Castle for atmosphere; Tigerlily on George Street for the budget. Gleneagles Townhouse on St Andrew Square for the canonical Edinburgh New Town design-luxury (already noted on August V5 Edinburgh Fringe); The Caledonian, A Waldorf Astoria at the West End for the canonical 1903 railway grand-dame.

**The Galley.** The Kitchin in Leith for the Michelin star; Ondine on George IV Bridge for North Sea seafood; The Devil’s Advocate up the Advocate’s Close for the after-show drink. Restaurant Martin Wishart in Leith for the canonical Edinburgh Michelin-starred modern Scottish; Number One at the Balmoral by chef Mark Donald for the canonical Edinburgh Michelin-starred fine-dining (the canonical Hogmanay-week destination).

**The Bearings.**

1. *Edinburgh Castle* (Edinburgh, Scotland, UK). The castle on the volcanic plug above the city, occupied since the Iron Age and besieged 26 times, more than any place in Britain; the Honours of Scotland and the Stone of Destiny kept in the Crown Room, the One O'Clock Gun still fired daily
2. *Calton Hill* (Edinburgh, Scotland, UK). The hill of the unfinished National Monument, the Athenian-temple replica abandoned for lack of funds in 1829 and kept as the city's beautiful failure; the Nelson Monument time-ball still drops at one o'clock each day as the One O'Clock Gun fires from the castle

### 13. Washington’s Crossing Reenactment

**Port:** Washington Crossing Historic Park, Pennsylvania
**Date:** Sat Dec 25
**Flags:** CULTURE

Christmas Day; the annual reenactment of Washington’s 1776 nighttime crossing of the ice-clogged Delaware in Durham boats, period-uniformed Continental Army reenactors push off from the Pennsylvania bank, ferry the Delaware against the current, land at McConkey’s Ferry on the New Jersey shore, and march toward the Trenton encampment. ### 14. Pirates in Paradise wraps the year

The six-day Pirates in Paradise Festival in Key West, Florida, held annually from December 27 through January 1, the year-closer for the global pirate-festival circuit. **Date:** Thu–Fri Dec 16–24
**Flags:** CULTURE, FOOD

The most iconic and most consequential Mexican Christmas tradition, observed annually for nine consecutive nights from December 16 through December 24 across Mexico and the wider Latin American diaspora. Las Posadas (Spanish for “the inns”) reenact the journey of Mary and Joseph from Nazareth to Bethlehem in search of lodging before the birth of Christ. The tradition was brought to New Spain in 1587 by Augustinian friars in Acolman, Mexico, who adapted the Spanish Christmas tradition into a missionary teaching tool for Indigenous Aztec converts. The nine nights correspond to the nine months of Mary’s pregnancy and the nine canonical Christian virtues. The signature elements: (1) the procession, each night a group of villagers walks through the neighborhood carrying images of Mary and Joseph, stopping at predetermined “posada” houses to sing the central posada song asking for lodging; (2) the call-and-response, the pilgrims outside sing the request for shelter, the homeowners inside sing the refusal, and after seven verses the door finally opens; (3) the seven-pointed star piñata, representing the seven deadly sins, broken at each posada; (4) the menu: tamales, atole or champurrado, buñuelos, and ponche navideño. The most spectacular contemporary observances are in San Miguel de Allende (the entire colonial center transformed nightly), Querétaro, and the village of Acolman where the tradition originated.

**The Berth.** In Mexico City: Las Alcobas; Four Seasons; Casa Habita. In San Miguel de Allende (3 hours north, the canonical Posadas pilgrimage city): Belmond Casa de Sierra Nevada for the canonical San Miguel heritage Relais & Châteaux luxury in the converted 16th-century mansions; Rosewood San Miguel de Allende for the canonical modern Mexican-luxury hilltop resort; Live Aqua Urban Resort San Miguel de Allende for the design-set modern boutique.

**The Galley.** In San Miguel de Allende: Moxi at Hotel Matilda by chef Enrique Olvera (Pujol’s sister) for the canonical San Miguel modern Mexican; The Restaurant by chef Donnie Masterton for the canonical San Miguel American-Mexican; La Posadita on Cuna de Allende for the canonical posadas-week traditional. In CDMX: Pujol, Quintonil, Rosetta, Maximo Bistrot. Festival- specific: tamales, atole, champurrado, buñuelos, and ponche navideño at every street vendor.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Historic Centre of Puebla* (Puebla, Mexico). The grid-plan colonial city of 1531, the cathedral's twin bell towers, the talavera-tile facades on every other house; UNESCO 1987, the city where mole poblano and chiles en nogada were both invented
2. *San Miguel de Allende* (Guanajuato, Mexico). The colonial silver-mining town of pink-stone Parroquia rising in neo-Gothic spires above the central plaza, the cobbled streets climbing the surrounding hills; UNESCO 2008, the heart of Mexican posadas tradition

---

### 16. Junkanoo

**Port:** Bay Street, Nassau, The Bahamas
**Date:** Boxing Day Dec 26 & New Year's Day Jan 1, 2028
**Flags:** CULTURE

The Bahamas’ national cultural festival and the most spectacular street parade in the Caribbean, observed annually on Boxing Day (December 26) and New Year’s Day (January 1) in Nassau, with the principal parade route on Bay Street through the historic center. The festival traces to the 17th-century African enslaved communities of New Providence Island, who were granted three days off at Christmas and used that time to stage parades in hand-built costumes of cardboard, crepe paper, and feathers. The name derives from “John Canoe,” the 17th-century West African enslaved leader who is the spiritual founder of the tradition. Signature elements: (1) the costume groups (Saxons, Valley Boys, One Family, Genesis Warhawks, Roots) construct elaborate themed costumes around a single theme announced in mid-November, with individual costumes taking 8–10 weeks of labor by 100+ artists per group; (2) the trademark Junkanoo rhythm section combines goatskin drums, cowbells, whistles, and brass horns into the unique beat that has defined Bahamian musical identity for 300 years; (3) the parades begin at 2 a.m. on Bay Street and continue through dawn, with judging at three points along the route. 30,000+ spectators line Bay Street; cruise ships dock in the harbor for the parade.

**The Berth.** In Nassau: The Ocean Club, A Four Seasons Resort on Paradise Island for the canonical Bahamas heritage luxury (where the James Bond Casino Royale was filmed); Atlantis Paradise Island for the canonical mega-resort luxury on Paradise Island (5-minute taxi to downtown Nassau and the parade route); Baha Mar resort complex on Cable Beach for the modern luxury alternative with the SLS, Rosewood, and Grand Hyatt options; The Graycliff Hotel in central Nassau in the converted 18th-century mansion for the canonical festival-route heritage boutique walking distance to Bay Street.

**The Galley.** In Nassau: Graycliff Restaurant in the converted 18th-century mansion for the canonical Bahamas heritage fine-dining (the 250,000-bottle wine cellar, the oldest in the Caribbean); Café Matisse on Bank Lane for the canonical Nassau modern Italian-Bahamian; Bahamian Cookin’ on Trinity Place for the canonical Bahamian home-style (the conch fritters and cracked conch); Twin Brothers at Arawak Cay’s “Fish Fry” for the canonical Nassau beach-fry.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Government House* (Nassau, The Bahamas). The pink-and-white colonial-Georgian residence of the Governor-General of the Bahamas on Mount Fitzwilliam above Nassau, completed 1737 and rebuilt 1929 after a hurricane; the 12-foot statue of Columbus on the front steps the work of an Italian sculptor in 1830
2. *Paradise Island Lighthouse* (Nassau, The Bahamas). The lighthouse on Paradise Island's western tip, oldest in the Bahamas at 1817 above the entrance to Nassau harbour, the white stone cylinder kept lit by a hand-pumped paraffin lamp until 1971; the harbour was a pirate refuge two centuries before the lighthouse went up

---

### 17. Holy Ship! Wrecked

**Port:** Hard Rock Hotel Riviera Maya, Yucatán, Mexico
**Date:** Wed–Sun mid-December, 4 nights
**Flags:** ART, FOOD

The legendary EDM destination festival, the closest thing electronic music has to a Burning-Man-style intentional community, with one of the most fanatically dedicated fanbases in dance music: the SHIPFAM. Founded by HARD/Insomniac, Cloud 9 Adventures, and The Bowery Presents in 2011 as a 4,000-capacity cruise out of Port Canaveral, calling at the Bahamas with an all-day private-island beach party, the festival ran on water for nine years. After the 2021 cancellation, the festival permanently moved ashore as Holy Ship! Wrecked, settling at the Hard Rock Hotel Riviera Maya. The land format kept everything that worked at sea and added six stage environments, Beach Stage, Main Stage, poolside pop-ups and three late-night venues, running sunset-to-sunrise across four days.

**The Berth.** On-property at Hard Rock Hotel Riviera Maya, the festival is the resort. Or UNICO 20°87° in Akumal forty minutes south for the alternative all-inclusive. Chablé Maroma, cenote-set jungle wellness retreat north of Tulum, the place to repair the damage the festival does; Nômade Holbox if extending the trip, rustic-chic on the beach, no shoes, no plan.

**The Galley.** On-resort dining is the festival itinerary. Off-property, Hartwood in Tulum (open-fire only, no electricity) and Casa Banana in Tulum for the canonical pre-festival dinner. Arca in Tulum, Jose Luis Hinostroza out of Noma, open fire, jungle plate; Kin Toh atop Azulik, treetop dining in a ceremonial-feeling space.

**The Bearings.**

1. *Chichén Itzá* (Tinúm, Yucatán, Mexico). The ninth-century Maya city raised in the dry Yucatán scrub, the Pyramid of Kukulcán climbing nine stages and 91 steps to the temple platform, the serpent-shadow on the staircase at each equinox; UNESCO 1988
2. *Tulum* (Tulum, Quintana Roo, Mexico). The walled Maya port of the thirteenth century perched on a 12-metre limestone cliff above the Caribbean, the Castillo overlooking the only navigable break in the Mesoamerican Reef; the wind through the small windows of the Temple of the Frescoes still smells of sea
